name: Astrojet (1960s retro)
description: Fuselage: Silver all over, the crown too. Cheatlines: A red cheatline under the windows, edged with a white and a thin navy pinstripe, that drops in a Z-shaped bolt ahead of the wing and runs on lower to a point at the nose. Tail: Light gray-white fin and fillet with the 1960s AA eagle roundel (red ring, white disc, blue 'A A' with eagle) and 'ASTROJET' in black capitals below it. Engines: Silver. Winglets: Silver. Nose cone: light gray-white. Titles: 'AMERICAN AIRLINES' in widely spaced dark-blue capitals above the windows; 'ASTROJET' small by the nose. Artwork: none. Colors hex: approximate.

notes: Re-checked 2026-11-15 on N905NN (2026-10-26): 'ASTROJET' on the fin is small, just above the root under the eagle disc (fin x 0.23-0.64, cap 0.05), not the large title first drawn; the nose title runs x 0.05-0.115; 'AMERICAN AIRLINES' x 0.24-0.73 as drawn. Shares read off a three-quarter view, so within about 0.02. Re-checked 2026-11-23 on N905NN (2026-10-26, 2021-09-22): the roundel is centred mid-chord about 0.4 up the fin (x 0.5, y 0.4), not high by the trailing edge. Re-checked 2026-11-27 on N905NN side-on at Los Angeles (2026-01-17): the crown is silver like the rest (it had been drawn white), and the cheatline is a red band about 0.2 m deep edged by a white and a thin navy pinstripe, not a red line over a blue one. Its bolt: the upper band ends in a point at x 0.163, the Z's stroke runs down and aft to x 0.21, and the lower band runs forward about 0.55-0.75 m under the centerline to a point at x 0.036 (it had been drawn about 0.35 m lower and thinner). The white pinstripe is drawn; the navy one outside it, a few centimeters wide, isn't. The nose title sits just above the lower band (x 0.048-0.104). The nose cone is painted a light gray-white like the fin, to x 0.034 (it had been drawn silver), and the dorsal fillet is white with the fin (it had taken the fuselage's color).
